title: T-107 Slice 4 — legacy-id reconciliation (aporrea/timing/apunta-v1/recolecta)
description: Slice 4 of the TASK-034 (GDD T-107) split — owns comment-2 carry-in (TASK-029 deferral). The four pre-GDD legacy microgame ids (aporrea, timing, apunta-v1, recolecta) map to NO canonical MECH_01-09 mechanic (recolecta especially has no home in the set). This slice decides and executes each id's fate individually. START WITH A PHASE-A DISPOSITION PROPOSAL (per-id: retire vs v2-native rewrite, with rationale mapped to the GDD mechanic set) for orchestrator ratification (human where a rewrite implies new gameplay) BEFORE implementation — do not guess. Then per id: a v2-native rewrite gets its own owned InputInterpreter (edge detection per §3.2; the 2-tick debounce-confirm delay is a real behavior change vs raw edges — retune tests); a retirement removes the un-debounced ButtonState.Pressed concern along with the code. NEVER port raw ButtonState.Pressed into a survivor. Wiring points: MicrogameHost.cs registry (Register calls), MicrogameContentGenerator.cs Specs + the 12 on-disk assets for whichever ids retire, and each id's existing test files. The MicrogameHost registry touch is compile-Unity-gated; Core-side rewrite/delete is fast-suite testable.
acceptance_criteria: A per-id disposition (retire vs v2-native rewrite) is proposed with GDD-mapped rationale and ratified before implementation; every one of aporrea/timing/apunta-v1/recolecta has a named, executed fate.

Any surviving/rewritten mechanic consumes InputInterpreter-derived edges (owned interpreter, §3.2), NOT raw ButtonState.Pressed; the un-debounced edge concern from TASK-029/TASK-023 is resolved for each id (by rewrite or by removal).
Retirements remove the id cleanly from the MicrogameHost registry, MicrogameContentGenerator Specs, and the on-disk assets, with no dangling references; the TASK-030 validator/migrator stays green.

Tests: rewrites are tdd with retuned debounce-aware expectations (documented, not blind-reblessed); retirements prove no production consumer references the removed id. Fast suite green; Framework registry compile verification rides the Unity gate.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
PHASE A RATIFIED (dev-t101 report, read-only, full GDD §4 + Annex D.1 + the 4 sources + wiring points read firsthand). Disposition: all 4 legacy ids RETIRE.

ORCHESTRATOR-RATIFIED (pure engineering, grounded in GDD Annex D.1 which has NO row for these ids + existing v2 implementations that supersede them): aporrea RETIRE (mash belongs to MECH_03 which has its own RunnerSim prototype; Aporrea's press-count race shares nothing with CORRE's endless-run — a 'rewrite to MECH_03' would be building CORRE from RunnerSim = a different already-tracked ticket, TASK-059); timing RETIRE (no MECH_XX matches single-tap-vs-moving-marker; closest cousin APUNTA's charge meter is already built as v2 MECH_04); apunta-v1 RETIRE (superseded — v2 MECH_04 ApuntaMicrogame is a full GDD-compliant implementation; id namespaces don't collide so it's a clean retirement, not a migration).

ROUTED TO HUMAN (genuine content/roadmap decision, not engineering): recolecta — maps to NO MECH_01-09; the §4.1 'Banco de reserva' names '¡RECOGE!' but that list is explicitly POST-prototype with no formula/AC/win-condition anywhere, so a 'rewrite' would be inventing a mechanic's design, not adapting to a spec. Asking the human: retire now (recoverable via git) vs keep the code live/wired as a ¡RECOGE! head-start. Recolecta never reads ButtonState.Pressed (confirmed) so its fate doesn't touch the TASK-029 debounce concern either way.

VACUOUS AC2 IS THE CORRECT OUTCOME (dev flagged, orchestrator confirms): under all-RETIRE, TASK-061 AC2 ('surviving/rewritten mechanic consumes InputInterpreter-derived edges') is satisfied vacuously — nothing survives as a rewrite, so there is no v2 InputInterpreter integration work in this slice. That is exactly what TASK-029's carry-in intended ('an explicit retirement removes the concern with the code'). The 3 real un-debounced consumers (Aporrea raw-count, Timing/Apunta-v1 latch) are all resolved by removal. Not forcing any into a v2 rewrite — that would invent a mechanic the GDD doesn't ask for.

EXECUTION: 2 units per dev recommendation. UNIT A = aporrea+timing+apunta-v1 retirement in ONE diff (mechanically identical 5-wiring-point pattern x3; tests-after via negative assertion = grep-proves no dangling reference + full suite green) — DISPATCHED NOW (ratified, disjoint from rev-t060's MECH_01 surface and the held MECH_03). UNIT B = recolecta, dispatched/dispositioned after the human rules. ADDED WIRING POINT (dev found, not in the ticket's list): Assets/Tests/PlayMode/Framework/MicrogamePoolIntegrationTests.cs references these ids by string (Unity-gated). SPLIT: Core .cs+test deletions + Specs source shrink + the MicrogameContentGeneratorSpecsTests regex-lock update are fast-suite-testable; MicrogameHost registry edits + the 4 View deletions + on-disk .asset deletions + GenerateAll/MigrateAll/ValidateAll + PlayMode MicrogamePoolIntegrationTests all ride the Unity gate. Do NOT touch ShapeFactory.cs (shared by Esquiva which stays).

So Unit A is now ALL 4 ids (aporrea+timing+apunta-v1+recolecta) in one diff. recolecta adds: RecolectaMicrogame.cs/RecolectaMicrogameTests.cs (Core, fast-suite), RecolectaView.cs+.meta (Framework, gated), MicrogameHost registry entry (gated), 3 Specs entries + 3 on-disk assets recolecta-d1-09/d2-10/d3-11+.meta (gated) — recolecta is the only one with 3 variants. recolecta is stick-only (no ButtonState.Pressed) so no debounce concern.
